chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abu Basir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman performing Tamattu' Hajj: if she enters the state of Ihram while pure, then menstruates before completing her Tamattu', she performs Sa'i but does not perform Tawaf until she becomes pure, then she completes her Tawaf, and her Tamattu' is complete. And if she enters Ihram while menstruating, she does not perform Sa'i, nor does she perform Tawaf until she becomes pure.

Thus, he (peace be upon him) clarified in this narration the correctness of what we mentioned, because he said: if she enters Ihram while pure, she performs Sa'i; and if she enters Ihram while menstruating, she does not perform Sa'i, nor does she perform Tawaf.

Had the meaning been what we mentioned, there would be no difference between the two states. The difference exists because when she enters Ihram while pure, it is permissible that her menstruation occurs after completing the Tawaf or after passing through half of it; at that time, it is permissible for her to advance the Sa'i and make up what remains of the Tawaf upon her.
But if she enters Ihram while menstruating, she has no way to perform any of the Tawaf, so consequently the Sa'i is also withheld. And this is clear, and praise be to Allah.
And that which also indicates that it is permissible for her to perform Sa'i if she has completed the Tawaf or has performed more than half of it.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَتْ: She entered the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the Hajj rulings for a woman who menstruates during Tamattu' Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar elucidates the distinction between *fard* (obligatory) and *nafl* (voluntary) components of Hajj rituals for menstruating women, a key topic in Shia fiqh. It establishes that entering Ihram in a state of purity allows for the performance of partial Tawaf, thereby validating the subsequent Sa'i, whereas entering while already menstruating invalidates the sequence entirely until purification. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of ritual purity as a prerequisite for the validity of specific Hajj acts.
